one_liner: Enterprise CRM platform for sales, service, marketing, and custom app development on the Salesforce Platform.
access_note: A free Developer Edition org with full REST/Bulk/Metadata API access can be self-registered instantly, though production API access for real business data typically requires a paid Enterprise Edition or above.
api_breadth_note: REST, Bulk 2.0, SOAP, Metadata, Streaming, and Connect APIs cover virtually every standard and custom object, plus flows/Apex actions via the new hosted MCP layer.
existing_mcp_note: Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers let any MCP client read/write records, run flows and Apex actions.

evidence.note: Official REST API developer guide confirming OAuth2 + connected apps model and broad resource coverage.
Official hosted MCP server docs, per-user OAuth2 with PKCE, CRUD/FLS/sharing enforced.

researcher_notes: Free Developer Edition is genuinely self-serve and API-complete for testing, which is why access is marked self_serve_free rather than gated_paid_plan — but a human should double check that this distinction (dev/test org vs. production org requiring Enterprise+) is acceptable for the intended use case.

one_liner: CRM and full-funnel marketing/sales/service software ('growth suite') with a large public API surface.
access_note: A free HubSpot CRM account lets you create a private app and get a bearer access token immediately with no sales contact, though private apps are not available in HubSpot's separate free 'developer test/portal' accounts.
api_breadth_note: CRM v3 objects (contacts, companies, deals, tickets, custom objects), engagements, marketing, CMS, and workflow APIs, documented across developers.hubspot.com.
existing_mcp_note: Official remote MCP server at mcp.hubspot.com (GA), plus a self-hosted @hubspot/mcp-server npm package and a one-click Claude connector.

evidence.note: Official docs confirming OAuth2 and private-app access-token auth methods.

researcher_notes: Community search results indicated some free/developer-portal HubSpot accounts cannot create private apps and must use OAuth instead — worth a human double-checking against the exact account type used for a prototype.

one_liner: Sales pipeline management CRM built around a visual deal pipeline, aimed at small and mid-size sales teams.
access_note: Free 14-day trial with no credit card required; a personal API token (x-api-token) is available immediately from account settings once signed up.
api_breadth_note: Deals, persons, organizations, pipelines/stages, activities, products, leads, and more, documented at developers.pipedrive.com/docs/api/v1.
existing_mcp_note: Pipedrive launched a native MCP server (June 2026) available to customers on all plans via secure OAuth.

evidence.note: Official auth docs describing x-api-token and OAuth2.
Official API reference showing broad resource coverage.

researcher_notes: None significant; Pipedrive is one of the more straightforward self-serve CRMs to build against today.

one_liner: Modern, highly customizable CRM built around a flexible data model of objects, records, and lists.
access_note: Attio has a free-forever plan (3 seats, 50,000 records) and API keys can be self-generated instantly under Workspace Settings > Developers.
api_breadth_note: Records, lists, objects/attributes, notes, tasks, comments, meetings, and workspace/reporting endpoints per docs.attio.com.
existing_mcp_note: Attio's hosted MCP server ships 37 tools across records, lists, notes, tasks, meetings, and reporting; available on all plans.

evidence.note: Official docs on OAuth2 and API-token authentication.

researcher_notes: Of the CRMs reviewed, Attio is the easiest to get a working AI-agent prototype against today given the free tier plus zero-friction API key + official hosted MCP.

one_liner: Open-source, self-hostable CRM positioned as an alternative to Salesforce/HubSpot, with a flexible custom-object data model.
access_note: The core product is open-source (AGPLv3) and free to self-host with no per-user fee; workspace-scoped API keys are generated directly in Settings > API & Webhooks with no approval step.
api_breadth_note: Core objects (People, Companies, Opportunities) plus auto-generated REST/GraphQL endpoints for any custom object, plus a separate Metadata API for schema management; no static reference since each workspace's schema differs.
existing_mcp_note: Multiple community MCP servers exist (e.g., github.com/jezweb/twenty-mcp); no official server from Twenty itself was found in this research.

evidence.note: Official API docs describing REST/GraphQL, API key generation, and per-workspace schema.
Official pricing page confirming free self-hosting.

researcher_notes: No official Twenty-branded MCP server was found — only community ones with varying maturity.

one_liner: Flexible, customizable work/project-management platform (usable as a lightweight CRM via custom 'apps'), owned by Progress Software.
access_note: Podio has a free-forever plan (up to 5 users, 100-item limit) and a Client ID/Secret + API key can be self-generated from account settings without manual approval, though restricted/higher-volume API operations require contacting support.
api_breadth_note: Apps, items, tasks, organizations/workspaces, comments, and files, documented at developers.podio.com; the platform is workspace/item-centric rather than a dedicated CRM object model.
existing_mcp_note: Progress (Podio's owner) runs an official hosted MCP server at mcp.podio.com with 22 tools, including a no-signup 'shared default credentials' quick-start mode.

evidence.note: Official Podio API authentication overview (OAuth2, multiple flows).
Official Progress/Podio documentation for the hosted MCP server.

researcher_notes: Surprising finding: despite Podio being a legacy platform now owned by Progress Software, it has one of the more AI-agent-friendly setups in this list.

one_liner: CRM module within the broader Zoho business-software suite, covering sales, pipeline, and automation.
access_note: A 15-day free trial requires no credit card, and OAuth2 'self-client' credentials for API access can be generated immediately in the Zoho API Console.
api_breadth_note: Core CRUD, Bulk Read/Write, Composite (batch up to 5 calls), COQL (SQL-like query language), Metadata, and Notification/webhook APIs.
existing_mcp_note: Zoho runs an official MCP platform (mcp.zoho.com) with four pre-built Zoho CRM MCP servers.

evidence.note: Official OAuth2 authentication overview for Zoho CRM API v8.

researcher_notes: The COQL (SQL-like query) API is unusually powerful for letting an AI agent construct flexible read queries.

one_liner: Sales CRM and engagement platform built for inside-sales teams, with calling, email, and SMS built directly into the product.
access_note: 'Try for Free' self-serve trial signup gives immediate access to Settings > Developer > API Keys (used via HTTP Basic Auth); there is no permanent free tier, only a trial before a paid plan is required.
api_breadth_note: Leads, contacts, opportunities, activities, sequences, bulk actions, reporting, webhooks, and a 30-day event log.
existing_mcp_note: Official MCP server at mcp.close.com/mcp (HTTP Streamable + OAuth2 Dynamic Client Registration).

evidence.note: Official docs on API-key (Basic Auth) authentication.

researcher_notes: Close's developer docs even offer to 'schedule a call' with the VP of Engineering about the API roadmap.

one_liner: CRM built natively inside Google Workspace, aimed at relationship-driven small and mid-size businesses.
access_note: Copper offers a free trial signup, after which an API key (X-PW-AccessToken header) can be self-generated under System Settings > API Keys; there is no standalone free-forever plan.
api_breadth_note: Leads, People, Companies, Opportunities, Projects, Tags, Tasks, Activities, Custom Fields, Related Items, File Upload, and Webhooks.
existing_mcp_note: Only third-party/community MCP servers found (e.g. Pipedream, Apideck); no official Copper-branded MCP server was located.

evidence.note: Official authentication docs (API Keys and OAuth2), and full resource menu confirming broad API breadth.

researcher_notes: Unlike most other CRMs in this list, Copper has no first-party MCP server despite a mature, broad REST API.

one_liner: Deal/relationship management CRM purpose-built for private equity, investment banking, and other private-markets firms, owned by Intapp.
access_note: There is no self-serve signup at all; API credentials can only be issued to an existing paying DealCloud customer whose admin enables the 'API' capability for a user group and generates a Client ID/API key/secret from a user profile.
api_breadth_note: Schema (EntryTypes/Fields/metadata), Cells and Rows data APIs (CRUD across all objects), User Management, real-time Publications/webhooks, Site Backups, Relationship Intelligence, and Template Reports.
existing_mcp_note: DealCloud MCP Server is in official client preview, documented at api.docs.dealcloud.com/mcp.
main_blocker: No self-serve account or credential creation — API/MCP access requires already being a paying DealCloud/Intapp customer with an admin role to provision credentials.

evidence.note: Official docs showing API keys require an admin-enabled user group with 'API' capability — i.e., an existing customer account.
Official DealCloud MCP Server docs (client preview).

researcher_notes: The API itself is technically broad and well-documented (including an official MCP preview), but real-world buildability is gated entirely by needing to already be a paying enterprise customer with admin rights.
